facts.text: The only player of the 1990s to rush for 1,000 yards at age 31 or older: James Brooks, 1990 — 1,004 yds at 32.
The only player of the 1990s to average 300 passing yards a game (8+ games): Warren Moon, 1990 — 312.6 per game.
The only player of the 1990s to post a passer rating of 110 (250+ attempts): Steve Young, 1994 — 112.8 rating.
Only two players of the 1990s rushed for 600 yards as a quarterback: Randall Cunningham (1990: 942 rush yds); Steve McNair (1997: 674 rush yds).
Only two players of the 1990s gained 1,000 receiving yards as a tight end: Ben Coates (1994: 1,174 yds, 96 rec); Shannon Sharpe (3×, best 1997: 1,107 yds, 72 rec).
Only two players of the 1990s scored 150 points: Gary Anderson (1998: 164 pts); Emmitt Smith (1995: 150 pts).
Only two players of the 1990s gained 1,000 receiving yards at age 22 or younger: Randy Moss (2×, best 1999: 1,413 yds at 22); Terry Glenn (1996: 1,132 yds at 22).
The only player of the 1990s to average 30 yards a kickoff return (20+ returns): Michael Bates, 1996 — 30.2 on 33 returns.
The only player of the 1990s to throw 30 touchdown passes and 20 interceptions: Brett Favre, 1998 — 31 TD, 23 INT.
The only player of the 1990s to gain 1,000 receiving yards on 50 or fewer catches: Michael Haynes, 1991 — 1,122 yds on 50 rec.
Only two players of the 1990s caught 90 passes for under 1,000 yards: Larry Centers (2×, best 1995: 101 rec, 962 yds); Haywood Jeffires (1992: 90 rec, 913 yds).
The only player of the 1990s to return 3 kickoffs for touchdowns: Mel Gray, 1994 — 3 KR TD.
Only two players of the 1990s completed 66% of their passes (250+ attempts): Steve Young (6×, best 1994: 70.3% on 461 att); Troy Aikman (1993: 69.1% on 392 att).
Only two players of the 1990s made 60 extra points: Jeff Wilkins (1999: 64-64 XP); Doug Brien (1994: 60-62 XP).
Just three players of the 1990s threw for 3,700 yards with 18 or fewer touchdowns: Warren Moon (1994: 4,264 yds, 18 TD); Dan Marino (1997: 3,780 yds, 16 TD); Jake Plummer (1998: 3,737 yds, 17 TD).
Just three players of the 1990s rushed for 1,800 yards: Barry Sanders (2×, best 1997: 2,053 yds); Terrell Davis (1998: 2,008 yds); Jamal Anderson (1998: 1,846 yds).

Just three players of the 1990s gained 2,200 yards from scrimmage: Marshall Faulk (2×, best 1999: 2,429 scrimmage yds); Barry Sanders (1997: 2,358 scrimmage yds); Terrell Davis (1998: 2,225 scrimmage yds).

Just three players of the 1990s rushed for 1,000 yards in 12 or fewer games: Olandis Gary (1999: 1,159 yds in 12 games); Barry Sanders (1993: 1,115 yds in 11 games); Rodney Hampton (1993: 1,077 yds in 12 games).
Only two players of the 1990s went a season without missing a field goal (15+ attempts): Gary Anderson (1998: 35-for-35); Tony Zendejas (1991: 17-for-17).
Only two players of the 1990s threw 20 touchdown passes at age 23 or younger: Peyton Manning (2×, best 1998: 26 TD at 22); Drew Bledsoe (1994: 25 TD at 22).
Only two players of the 1990s scored 22 touchdowns: Emmitt Smith (2×, best 1995: 25 TD); Terrell Davis (1998: 23 TD).
Only two players of the 1990s ran for 8 touchdowns as a quarterback: Kordell Stewart (1997: 11 rush TD); Steve McNair (2×, best 1997: 8 rush TD).
Only two players of the 1990s threw a touchdown on 8% of their passes (250+ attempts): Kurt Warner (1999: 8.2% (41 TD)); Randall Cunningham (1998: 8% (34 TD)).
Just three players of the 1990s caught 80 passes as a running back: Marshall Faulk (2×, best 1999: 87 rec, 1,048 yds); Derek Loville (1995: 87 rec, 662 yds); Keith Byars (1990: 81 rec, 819 yds).
Only two players of the 1990s intercepted 7 passes at age 33 or older: James Hasty (1999: 7 INT at 34); Rod Woodson (1999: 7 INT at 34).

Just four players of the 1990s got sacked 55 times: Randall Cunningham (1992: sacked 60 times); Jeff George (2×, best 1997: sacked 58 times); Tim Couch (1999: sacked 56 times); Drew Bledsoe (1999: sacked 55 times).

Just four players of the 1990s averaged 46 yards a punt (40+ punts): Craig Hentrich (1998: 47.2 avg on 69); Greg Montgomery (1992: 46.9 avg on 53); Tom Rouen (2×, best 1998: 46.9 avg on 66); John Kidd (1996: 46.3 avg on 78).

Just four players of the 1990s threw 35 touchdown passes: Kurt Warner (1999: 41 TD, 13 INT); Brett Favre (3×, best 1996: 39 TD, 13 INT); Steve Beuerlein (1999: 36 TD, 15 INT); Steve Young (2×, best 1998: 36 TD, 12 INT).
Just three players of the 1990s threw 25 interceptions: Peyton Manning (1998: 28 INT, 26 TD); Drew Bledsoe (1994: 27 INT, 25 TD); Bobby Hebert (1996: 25 INT, 22 TD).
Just three players of the 1990s ran for 18 touchdowns: Emmitt Smith (3×, best 1995: 25 rush TD); Terry Allen (1996: 21 rush TD); Terrell Davis (1998: 21 rush TD).
Just three players of the 1990s recorded 12 sacks at age 23 or younger: Derrick Thomas (1990: 20 sacks at 23); Jevon Kearse (1999: 14.5 sacks at 23); Simeon Rice (1996: 12.5 sacks at 22).

method: NFL before 2000: each line is one Stathead (Pro Football Reference) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; the result rows, with Pro Football Reference's stable player ids, are stored as provenance. Nothing recalled or estimated.

Passing, rushing and receiving are official from 1932, interceptions from 1940, sacks from 1982 (Pro Football Reference's unofficial earlier sack counts are excluded); rules on a category a decade did not record simply return nothing. The 1960s include AFL seasons, which NFL records count; the 1940s exclude the AAFC, which they do not.
